entry.dc:title: On the Method of Calculation of the Upper Structure of Permanent Open-Pit Mine Tracks.
entry.dc:creator: Volkov G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: Recently, the traction units of the PE-2, PE-2M and Ye-10 type with motor dump-cars, with 31 t load per axle, have been put into operation at open-pit mines in the USSR. In this connection it became necessary to investigate the conditions of operation of the existing upper structure of permanent tracks under high axial loads. The article describes an experiment designed to measure the stress in the upper structure of the track in the access trench to the Sarbay open pit ore mine in Kazakhstan. As a result, the method of calculating the strength of the track, built on wooden and on reinforced concrete ties, has been corrected. Possible designs of reinforced concrete slabs are shown.

entry.dc:title: Driving an Inclined Trench for the Skip Hoist at the Sibay Open-Pit Mine.
entry.dc:creator: Khokhryakov V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The experience of driving an inclined trench for a skip hoist of Sibay open-put copper ore mine is generalized. The lifting capacity of the skip is 40 t, maximum depth of the hoist - 380m, the gradient - 39 degree , maximum hoist speed - 8. 2 m/s. The length of the trench (first stage) to the depth of 180m is 286m, its bottom width - 14. 5m, top width - 28 to 65m. It is to be equipped with two rail tracks 3. 07m wide each. The drilling and blasting work and the technology of stoping of the steep skip trench are described in detail. Recommendations are given for improving the technology of driving an inclined trench.

entry.dc:title: Determination of a Rational Direction of Deepening an Open-Pit Mine by Graphs of Isolines of Specific Return.
entry.dc:creator: Zagoruiko G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: A method is set forth for determining a rational direction of deepening an open pit mine by using the example of a deposit of silicate nickel ores in the Urals, characterized by a variety of forms and condition of bedding of ore bodies. The problem is solved by the method of variants in two stages. Plane problems are solved by means of geometric mine graphs of isolines of specific return. The spatial problem is solved by means of a longitudinal section of the pit on which the lines of the transverse sections are imposed, indicating the gain at the level of the calculated horizons when lowering the mining operations in accordance with the rational direction found for the plane problem. The variants of the pit deepening are evaluated by the summary reduced gain, taking into account the factor of time and the capital investment efficiency coefficient.

entry.dc:title: Solving the Static Problem of Determination of the Boundaries of Open-Pit Mines.
entry.dc:creator: Atamas P.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The existing principles of static determination of open-pit mine limits are considered and a new principle is proposed, based on comparing the mean weighted boundary coefficient and the mean exploitation coefficient of overburden stripping. It is shown that application of the principle permits fuller utilization of possibilities and an expansion of the field of application of the open-pit method of mining.

entry.dc:title: Determination of Rational Direction of the Sinking of an Open-Pit Mine by the Method of Proportioning of the Working Zone.
entry.dc:creator: Evsin V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: A new method is described concerning the shaping of the open-pit area in accordance with generally accepted criteria by means of proportional correlation of the parameters of the working zone. The direction of the sinking of thepit is determined by the equation of minimal relations of projections of the open pit working zones as to the rock volume and ore at different pit edges. The dependences obtained are valid for ore and several ore bodies separated by rock layers. The use of this method does not involve the measuring of the areas by a planimeter on geological sections and approximation of the contours of the deposit and of the pit, it sharply reduces the volume of calculations. The method can be easily realized on a computer. It has been practically tested at Sarbay open-pit mine in Kazakhstan.

entry.dc:title: Synthesis of Optimal Technological Schemes of Open-Pit Mine Workings.
entry.dc:creator: Lepilkin N.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: An attempt is made to formulate and to outline the ways of solving the problem of synthesis of optimal technological schemes of open pit mine workings using continuous action technology. On the basis of an analysis of the features of some of the main such technological schemes, a series of structural parameters are established, defining the class of the discussed technological schemes in an identical way. Introduction of structural parameters enables the synthesis problem to be reduced to that of nonlinear integer-value programming. A method is proposed for the determination of the optimum values of the parameters, based on the principle of self-instruction.

entry.dc:title: Artificial Ventilation of Deep Open-Pit Mines.
entry.dc:creator: Veselov A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The existing and proposed mobile installations for the ventilation of deep open-pit mines by means of free turbulent streams show considerable drawbacks and are unsuitable for this task. Only the lower part of the open-pit mine, and not its entire volume, should be ventilated. For this purpose, suction ventilating installations with modern centrifugal ventilation mounted on the surface of the open-pit mine, should be used. They should be equipped with strongly-built suction air ducts laid on the edge of the open-pit mine and extending to its bottom.

entry.dc:title: TWIN BUTTES. A DEEP LOW-GRADE COPPER PRODUCER
entry.dc:creator: CALDWELL AB
entry.dc:description: At Twin Buttes near Tucson, Ariz, the Anaconda Co has recently completed the largest earth-moving task so far undertaken in the mining industry, removing 235 million tons of rock and overburden to uncover a complex deposit of ore grading slightly over 0. 5% copper and lying between 600 and 800 ft beneath the surface. How and why this was done, and what the results have been so far are set forth in detail in this survey of the complete operation at Anaconda's huge new open-pit mine. Article describes the equipment used, maintenance program by which down time is minimized and the methods by which mining and milling are accomplished. It also gives background detail in this survey of the complete operation atAnaconda's huge new openpit mine. Article describes the equipment used, maintenance program by which down time is minimized and the methods by which mining and milling are accomplished. It also gives background details on the geology and discovery of the orebody.

entry.dc:title: MAINTENANCE OF LARGE SHOVESL IN OPEN-PIT MINING AT QUEBEC CARTIER
entry.dc:creator: PROULX GP
entry.dc:description: Quebec Cartier Mining Company operates ten 8-cu yd electric shovels to extract iron ore from its open-pit mine in northern Quebec, where the temperature has averaged 27 F during the past 9 yr. Experience gained since the start of operations in 1959 has shown the need for sound equipment specifications designed to meet the existing mining conditions along with constant training of manpower and engineering assistance to improve operating costs and equipment availability.

entry.dc:title: OPEN-PIT PLANNING USING A COMPUTER
entry.dc:creator: BOYCE WP
entry.dc:description: A system is described which uses a computer to determine the annual extraction sequence and final excavation extent of an existing, or a proposed open-pit mine. This system uses estimates of capital and operating costs for a range of annual outputs of ore and waste materials, and the physical properties of the potential pit area, to calculate ranges of unit costs and associated pit extents. It determines the scale of operations and final pit extent which would give maximum net monetary return, and then assesses the profitability of this return.

entry.dc:title: The porphyry copper deposit exposed in the liberty open-pit mine near Ely, Nevada. Part II. the formation of hydro-thermal alteration zones
entry.dc:creator: Fournier R.
entry.dc:description: In the southwest part of the Liberty pit a large porphyry body exhibits a zonal alteration pattern related to fissures and pyrite-bearing veins. The outermost zone contains unaltered K-feldspar, kaolinite after plagioclase, and black biotite after hornblende. An intermediate zone contains reconstituted K-feldspar, phlogopitic biotite, and muscovite or muscovite plus K-feldspar replacing only plagioclase. In the innermost zone the only silicates are quartz and muscovite. In some places an alteration band of K-feldspar after plagioclase separates kaolinite and muscovite. The widespread association of kaolinite and K-feldspar in hydro-thermal alteration zones suggests that these two minerals were stable together at the time of formation. Experimental data show that, where quartz controls the activity of silica in solution, kaolinite and K-feldspar should react to form muscovite. However, calculations predict that, at 15,000 psi, solutions with silica activities compatible with amorphous or gelatinous silica could stabilize K-feldspar and kaolinite relative to muscovite at temperatures below about 250° C. The rapid decomposition either of plagioclase feldspar or montmorillonite is considered a prime cause for the attainment of such high activities of silica in pore solutions of rock. The supersaturation of pore solutions with silica is a transient condition; quartz precipitates where kaolinite and K-feldspar react to give muscovite. Thus, the zonally distributed alteration at Ely is considered to have taken place after the rock had cooled to below 250° C. In contrast, the diffusely distributed muscovite and montmorillonite found in another portion of the pit probably commenced at 600° to 700° C with only minor formation of alteration products below 250° C. © 1967 Society of Economic Geologists, Inc.

entry.dc:title: The porphyry copper deposit exposed in the liberty open-pit mine near Ely, Nevada. Part I. Syngenetic formation
entry.dc:creator: Fournier R.
entry.dc:description: Detailed mapping- of the Liberty open-pit copper mine indicates that a monzonite porphyry complex was emplaced into a folded sedimentary sequence during active faulting in Cretaceous time. The upper portion of the intruded igneous material was the first to solidify and at times mobile mushes of plagioclase, hornblende, and biotite crystals in a viscous groundmass were injected along lines of rupture into already solid and altered upper portions of the same igneous body. Alteration of the upper part of the porphyry complex took place simultaneously with the continued injection and crystallization of magma from deeper in the system. First, K-feldspar partly replaced plagioclase and later, muscovite replaced most of the remaining plagioclase. Phlogopitic biotite containing rutile replaced hornblende and iron-rich biotite. This alteration preceded the final emplacement of a second, comagmatic portion of the rock which in turn exhibits an alteration suite mainly composed of iron-rich biotite, montmorillonite, and the zeolites, chabazite and stilbite. The distribution of sulfides in igneous rocks and immediately adjacent sediments suggests that the sulfides originated in the porphyries and locally escaped into the surrounding rock as the porphyries crystallized. Most chalcopyrite, the main primary copper-bearing mineral, is distributed as grains in the groundmass with no trace of alignment along earlier cracks. The groundmass which contains the chalcopyrite is composed mainly of aplitic-textured K-feldspar and quartz, and it formed at the time of the original crystallization of the rock and not as a result of later alteration processes. In some rocks the groundmass K-feldspar contains a greater proportion of potassium than does coexisting phenocryst K-feldspar. If a dense aqueous pore fluid had been present during the cooling history of the rock these feldspars should have equilibrated by base exchange of Na+ and K+. It is postulated that the formation of hydrous alteration products after feldspar and hornblende may effectively have kept the fugacity of water low in the porphyry as it cooled so that only an attenuated gas phase existed in the pores of the rock. © 1967 Society of Economic Geologists, Inc.
